title: FreeRTOS on ESP32: Arduino and ESP-IDF

spans.text: LESSON PURPOSE

Goal: apply “FreeRTOS on ESP32: Arduino and ESP-IDF” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Queues pass messages and decouple tasks. In a project, follow this guidance: Protect mutable data shared between tasks with synchronization or message queues.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.
EXAMPLE CODE
EXPECTED RESULT
Task creation can fail when memory is unavailable; stack size and priority need target-specific review.
CORE EXPLANATION
ESP-IDF uses FreeRTOS tasks and queues to separate work. Measure stack, priority, affinity, and blocking; a stalled task may trigger a watchdog.
IMPORTANT LINE BREAKDOWN
Key line:
xTaskCreate(worker, "worker", 2048, nullptr, 1, nullptr);

What it does: Queues pass messages and decouple tasks.
Why it is used: Protect mutable data shared between tasks with synchronization or message queues.
If omitted or changed: Do not hide a stall by disabling the watchdog; diagnose why the task stopped progressing.
